{{primary sources|date=February 2016}}
In mathematics, the '''Bhatia–Davis inequality''', named after [[Rajendra Bhatia]] and [[Chandler Davis]], is an [[upper bound]] on the [[variance]] ''σ''<sup>2</sup> of any bounded [[probability distribution]] on the real line.

Despite its name, the inequality had previously been found by Muilwijk,<ref name="muilwijk1966"> {{Cite journal |last=Muilwijk |first=J. |date=1966 |title=Note on a Theorem of M. N. Murthy and V. K. Sethi |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25051569 |journal=Sankhyā: The Indian Journal of Statistics, Series B (1960-2002) |volume=28 |issue=1/2 |pages=183–183 |issn=0581-5738}}</ref> based on Murthy and Sethi,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Murthy |first=M. N. |last2=Sethi |first2=V. K. |date=1965 |title=Self-Welighting Design at Tabulation Stage |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25051541 |journal=Sankhyā: The Indian Journal of Statistics, Series B (1960-2002) |volume=27 |issue=1/2 |pages=201–210 |issn=0581-5738}}</ref> 34 years before publication of the better-known article by Bhatia and Davis.<ref name="bhatia2000">{{Cite journal|last1=Bhatia|first1=Rajendra|last2=Davis|first2=Chandler|date=2000|title=A Better Bound on the Variance|url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00029890.2000.12005203|journal=The American Mathematical Monthly|language=en|volume=107|issue=4|pages=353–357|doi=10.1080/00029890.2000.12005203|s2cid=38818437 |issn=0002-9890|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

{{TOC limit}}

== Statement ==
Let ''m'' and M be the lower and upper bounds, respectively, for a set of real numbers ''a<sub>1</sub>'', ..., ''a<sub>n</sub> ,'' with a particular [[probability distribution]]. Let ''μ'' be the [[expected value]] of this distribution.

Then the Bhatia–Davis inequality states:

: <math> \sigma^2 \le (M - \mu)(\mu - m). \, </math>

Equality holds if and only if every ''a<sub>j</sub>'' in the set of values is equal either to ''M'' or to ''m''.<ref name="muilwijk1966"/><ref name="bhatia2000"/>

<!--
A  lower bound for the variance based on the Bhatia&ndash;Davis inequality has been found by Agarwal et al.<ref name=Agarwal2005>Agarwal R P, Barnett N S, Cerone P and Dragomir S S (2005) "A survey on some inequalities for expectation and variance." ''Computers and mathematics with applications'' 49 (2005) 429–480</ref>

: <math> ( M - \mu )( \mu - m ) - \frac{ ( M - m )^3 } 6 \le \sigma^2 </math> -->
==Proof==
Since <math>m \leq A \leq M</math>, 

<math>0 \leq \mathbb{E}[(M - A)(A - m)] = -\mathbb{E}[A^2] - m M + (m+M)\mu</math>.

Thus, 

<math> \sigma^2 = \mathbb{E}[A^2] - \mu^2 \leq - m M + (m+M)\mu - \mu^2 = (M - \mu) (\mu - m)</math>.

== Extensions of the Bhatia–Davis inequality ==
If <math>\Phi</math> is a positive and unital linear mapping of a ''C* -''algebra <math>\mathcal{A}</math> into a ''C*'' -algebra <math>\mathcal{B}</math>, and ''A'' is a self-adjoint element of <math>\mathcal{A}</math> satisfying ''m'' <math>\leq</math> ''A'' <math>\leq</math> ''M'', then:

<math>\Phi (A^2)-(\Phi A)^2\leq (M-\Phi A)(\Phi A - m)</math>.

If <math>\mathit{X}</math> is a discrete random variable such that

<math>P (X=x_i)=p_i,</math> where <math>i = 1, ..., n</math>, then:

<math>s_p^2=\sum_{1}^n p_ix_i^2-(\sum_{1}^n p_ix_i)^2\leq(M-\sum_{1}^n p_ix_i)(\sum_{1}^n p_ix_i-m)</math>,

where <math>0\leq p_i \leq1</math> and <math>\sum_{1}^n p_i=1</math>.

== Comparisons to other inequalities ==
The Bhatia–Davis inequality is stronger than [[Popoviciu's inequality on variances]] (note, however, that Popoviciu's inequality does not require knowledge of the expectation or mean), as can be seen from the conditions for equality. Equality holds in Popoviciu's inequality if and only if half of the ''a<sub>j</sub>''  are equal to the upper bounds and half of the ''a<sub>j</sub>''  are equal to the lower bounds. Additionally, Sharma<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Sharma|first=Rajesh|date=2008|title=Some more inequalities for arithmetic mean, harmonic mean and variance|journal=Journal of Mathematical Inequalities|issue=1|pages=109–114|doi=10.7153/jmi-02-11|issn=1846-579X|doi-access=free}}</ref> has made further refinements on the Bhatia–Davis inequality.
